text: Restricting the student's fine-tune to a low-rank adapter (LoRA rank 16) was evaluated in a weak-to-strong setup with gpt2-medium as the weak supervisor and mistral-7b as the strong student, across 10 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.48 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling, when trained on ground truth, was 0.75. Under weak supervision the adapter-constrained student reached a transfer accuracy of 0.69 (SE 0.02), corresponding to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.78 with a standard error of 0.09. This compares with a baseline PGR of 0.13; the observed PGR exceeds the baseline by more than two standard errors, so the low-rank constraint appears to recover substantially more of the weak-to-strong gap than the unconstrained baseline. Caveats: no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, nor for the weak and strong accuracies, and the finding rests on a single task and model pair, so generality beyond this configuration is untested.
